REASONING:
Step 1 – Frame the project  
- **Objective:** Improve quality of school education and increase access to science & commerce senior‑secondary education in Chhattisgarh.  
- **Scope & Components:** Four Results Areas – (RA‑1) teacher professional development, (RA‑2) student diagnostic & remedial systems, (RA‑3) model composite school development, (RA‑4) school leadership. Includes IPF‑TA technical assistance, EMIS development, procurement of civil works, training modules, and monitoring.  
- **Delivery Model:** State Implementation Society for Samagra Shiksha (SIS‑SS) as nodal implementer; sub‑implementers SCERT, SIEMAT, DIETs, PWD, RES; Project Management Consultant (PMC) and Independent Verification Agency (IVA) engaged.  
- **Timeline:** July 2023 – December 2028 (5 years).  
- **Budget:** Total operation US$558.3 M; CHALK programme US$535.8 M; IBRD loan US$300 M; counterpart US$258.3 M.  
- **Key Stakeholders:** GoCG (DoSE, DoSE&L), SCERT, SIEMAT, DIETs, PWD, RES, teachers, school management committees, students, World Bank, PMC, IVA, technical service providers.  
- **External Dependencies:** Climate variability (droughts/floods), COVID‑19 recovery, coal‑mining block transition, e‑procurement platforms (e‑GP, GeM), state EMIS rollout, possible changes in personal‑data legislation.

Step 2 – Category sweep (candidate risks with supporting text)  
- Technical: EMIS capacity, digital‑assessment rollout, data‑loss risk.  
- Financial: Fiduciary risk assessed as “Substantial”.  
- Schedule: Construction delays due to climate, AWP&B approval lag, procurement‑plan absence.  
- Stakeholder: Teacher shortage & inadequate training; high boy dropout; weak grievance redress; lack of residential schools for boys.  
- Political/Regulatory: New personal‑data law impact; anti‑corruption compliance; procurement rule changes.  
- Environmental: Construction waste, pollution, lack of green‑building, fire‑safety gaps.  
- Organizational: SIS‑SS staffing at 70 %; coordination among multiple agencies; internal‑audit weaknesses.  
- External: Climate‑induced attendance loss, broader climate change threats.

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All listed risks are directly quoted in the appraisal document (see evidence excerpts below).

Step 4 – Assess & mitigate  

| Risk | Likelihood (1‑5) | Impact (1‑5) | Mitigation (concise) |
|------|------------------|--------------|----------------------|
| R01 Technical – EMIS/assessment digitalisation capacity | 3 | 4 | Recruit/assign dedicated IT staff, provide capacity‑building for SCERT/SAC, set phased delivery milestones with external technical assistance. |
| R02 Financial – Fiduciary risk (Substantial) | 3 | 5 | Strengthen internal controls, establish audit committee, conduct regular FM/Procurement trainings, use independent verification reports. |
| R03 Schedule – Climate‑related construction delays | 3 | 3 | Incorporate disaster‑resilient designs, build time buffers, monitor weather forecasts, adjust work plans proactively. |
| R04 Stakeholder – Teacher shortage & inadequate in‑service training | 4 | 4 | Accelerate recruitment, use blended (online/offline) TaRL courses, provide incentives, monitor teacher‑to‑class ratios. |
| R05 Stakeholder – High dropout of adolescent boys (no residential schools) | 4 | 3 | Finance residential facilities for boys in model schools, offer scholarships/conditional cash transfers, community mobilisation. |
| R06 Organizational – No annual procurement plan | 3 | 3 | Develop and publish a yearly procurement plan aligned with AWP&B, train procurement staff, use e‑GP/STEP tracking. |
| R07 Technical – Data loss from climate‑induced incidents | 2 | 3 | Implement cloud‑based backups, redundant servers, and a disaster‑recovery protocol for EMIS and assessment data. |
| R08 Environmental – Construction waste, pollution, lack of green standards | 3 | 3 | Enforce waste‑segregation, adopt green‑building guidelines, monitor compliance, include EHS clauses in contracts. |
| R09 Stakeholder – Weak grievance redress & facility‑maintenance mechanisms | 3 | 3 | Strengthen GRM with clear escalation, regular community‑led social audits, publish response timelines. |
| R10 Political/Regulatory – New personal‑data protection legislation | 2 | 4 | Monitor legal developments, conduct impact analysis, update data‑handling procedures, train staff on compliance. |
| R11 Organizational – SIS‑SS operating at 70 % of sanctioned staff | 3 | 3 | Fill vacancies promptly, use temporary contracts, re‑allocate staff from less‑critical functions. |
| R12 Organizational – Coordination challenges among multiple agencies | 3 | 3 | Set up a joint coordination unit, hold monthly steering meetings, define clear roles/RACI matrix. |
| R13 Political/Regulatory – Corruption / anti‑corruption compliance risk | 2 | 5 | Apply World Bank anti‑corruption guidelines, enforce whistle‑blower protection, conduct independent audits, vet contractors. |
| R14 Schedule – Delayed AWP&B approval (3‑5 months into FY) | 3 | 3 | Prepare draft AWP&B early, engage finance ministry for pre‑approval, align fund‑release schedules with project milestones. |
| R15 External – Climate change reducing school attendance | 3 | 3 | Develop climate‑resilient school calendars, expand remote‑learning options, establish early‑warning systems for extreme weather. |

Step 5 – Consolidate  
All 15 risks are distinct and directly supported by the appraisal document; no duplicates remain.
